lessons.title: What Is a Minibeast?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name at least three minibeasts.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at pictures of common minibeasts.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss and name minibeasts found in the garden (snail, ladybird, worm, spider, ant), noting they are small creatures.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note minibeast vocabulary — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Look for minibeasts in your garden or a park together.

lessons.title: Story Time: 'The Bad-Tempered Ladybird' by Eric Carle
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe how the ladybird's mood changes.
lessons.main_activity: Read the story, discussing the ladybird's bad mood and how the day unfolds.

differentiation.extension: Discuss the story's message about being polite

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension and emotional understanding — evidence for LIT.1/PSED.1.
lessons.plenary: Discuss ways to be polite even when grumpy.
lessons.home_link: Talk about how to stay calm when feeling grumpy.

lessons.title: Counting Ladybird Spots
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count spots on ladybird pictures accurately up to 10.
lessons.starter_activity: Count spots on a ladybird picture together.
lessons.main_activity: Children count and add a given number of spot stickers to paper ladybirds, checking accuracy.
key_questions: How many spots does your ladybird have?
Can you count them again to check?

differentiation.extension: Count to 10+ and compare with a partner

lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting accuracy — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.home_link: Count spots or dots on objects at home.

lessons.title: Making a Symmetrical Ladybird Craft
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create a symmetrical pattern of spots on a ladybird craft.
lessons.main_activity: Children make a ladybird craft, adding spots symmetrically on both wings.
resources_needed: Red/black paper, spot stickers or paint
key_questions: Is your pattern the same on both sides?
How many spots on each wing?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe symmetry understanding and fine motor skill — evidence for EAD.1/MATHS.2.
lessons.home_link: Look for symmetry in minibeasts or objects at home.

lessons.title: Minibeast Hunt
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to find and identify minibeasts in an outdoor environment.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss where minibeasts like to hide (under logs, in soil).
lessons.main_activity: Go on a minibeast hunt in the outdoor area using magnifying glasses and bug pots, identifying and gently observing any minibeasts found.

differentiation.support: Adult supports the search and identification
differentiation.extension: Identify multiple minibeasts and describe their features

lessons.assessment_notes: Note investigative and identification skill — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Share minibeasts found (then return them gently to their habitat).
lessons.home_link: Go on a minibeast hunt in your garden or a park together.

lessons.title: Phonics Consolidation: Reading Minibeast Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read simple minibeast-themed words.
lessons.main_activity: Phonics stations reading minibeast-themed word cards and simple sentences (e.g. 'the bug is on a web').

differentiation.support: Read simple CVC words with support

lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application to themed vocabulary — evidence for LIT.2.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading minibeast words over the week.

lessons.title: Counting Spider Legs
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count in a repeated group (legs of 8 for spiders).
lessons.starter_activity: Recap counting in twos from Week 12.
lessons.main_activity: Children count spider legs (8 per spider) using counters, and count multiple spiders' legs together.
key_questions: How many legs does one spider have?
How many legs do two spiders have altogether?

differentiation.extension: Count legs of 2-3 spiders and add totals

lessons.assessment_notes: Note counting in groups understanding — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of spider leg counting.
lessons.home_link: Count legs on toy insects or pictures at home.

lessons.title: Moving Like Minibeasts
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to move imaginatively like different minibeasts.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss how a snail moves slowly vs a spider scuttles.
lessons.main_activity: Children move around the space imitating snails crawling slowly, spiders scuttling, and butterflies fluttering.
key_questions: Can you scuttle like a spider?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe imaginative movement — evidence for EAD.2/PD.1.
lessons.home_link: Act out a minibeast movement for family.

lessons.title: Where Do Minibeasts Live?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe a minibeast's habitat.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the minibeast hunt from Tuesday.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss and match minibeasts to their habitats (worm-soil, spider-web, woodlouse-under a log) using picture cards.
key_questions: Why does a spider live in a web?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note habitat understanding — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Look for minibeast habitats (under stones, in soil) together.

lessons.title: Writing Minibeast Labels
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to attempt to write a simple label for a minibeast.
lessons.main_activity: Children draw a minibeast and attempt to write its name using known phonics sounds.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note writing progress — evidence for LIT.3.
lessons.plenary: Share labelled minibeast pictures with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Draw and label a minibeast together at home.

lessons.title: Sorting Minibeasts: With Wings or Without
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to sort minibeasts using one criterion.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss which minibeasts have wings (butterfly, ladybird) vs not (worm, snail).
lessons.main_activity: Children sort mixed minibeast picture cards into 'has wings' and 'no wings' groups, counting each.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note sorting and counting skill — evidence for MATHS.2/MATHS.1.
lessons.home_link: Sort toy minibeasts or pictures into groups at home.

lessons.title: Are Minibeasts Helpful?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe one way a minibeast helps the environment.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what bees do for flowers.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss how minibeasts like bees (pollination) and worms (soil health) help the environment.
key_questions: How does a bee help flowers?
How does a worm help the soil?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note early ecological understanding — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap how minibeasts help the environment.
lessons.home_link: Talk about why we should look after minibeasts at home.

lessons.title: Retelling 'The Bad-Tempered Ladybird'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retell the story's key events in sequence.
lessons.main_activity: Using picture cards, children retell the story sequence using sequencing words.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note sequencing and retelling ability — evidence for LIT.1/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: One group retells to the class.
lessons.home_link: Retell the story to someone at home.

lessons.title: Number Bonds Recap: Minibeast Theme
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall number bonds to 10 using a minibeast-themed activity.
lessons.main_activity: Using ladybird/bug counters, children practise and record all number bonds to 10.
key_questions: What are all the ways to make 10?
Can you recall this without counting?
lessons.assessment_notes: Assess number bond to 10 fluency — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of all bonds to 10.
lessons.home_link: Practise number bonds to 10 with any small objects at home.

lessons.title: Minibeasts Recap Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about minibeasts learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: Contribute to a class 'Minibeasts' display summarising minibeast names, habitats, and their helpful roles.
key_questions: What have we learned about minibeasts?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about minibeasts with your family.

lessons.title: Phonics Review: Minibeast Reading Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read minibeast-themed sentences fluently.
lessons.main_activity: Phonics stations reading a range of minibeast-themed sentences with increasing fluency.
key_questions: Can you read it more quickly?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note reading fluency progress — evidence for LIT.2.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading minibeast sentences over the weekend.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Counting, Sorting, Number Bonds
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply counting, sorting, and number bond skills learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: Rotate through 3 stations: counting spots/legs, sorting minibeasts by wings, number bonds to 10.
key_questions: Which group does this belong to?
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising sorting and counting over the weekend.

lessons.title: Minibeasts Celebration Performance
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to combine movement and craft in a short class performance.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all elements learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: Whole-class performance combining minibeast movements from Tuesday, with ladybird crafts displayed.
key_questions: What was your favourite part of this week?
How did it feel to perform?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe confidence and enjoyment — evidence for EAD.2.
lessons.plenary: Round of applause; recap the minibeasts week.
lessons.home_link: Perform a minibeast movement for family this weekend.
